question.problem:
Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD},$ given the points $A(3,1,2),$ $B(0,5,0),$ $C(3,3,1),$ and $D(1,4,2).$

$V=${{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(5j)-(3i+1j+2k) \\  & =-3i+4j-2k \\  & =⟨-3,4,-2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(3i+3j+1k)-(3i+1j+2k) \\  & =2j-1k \\  & =⟨0,2,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(1i+4j+2k)-(3i+1j+2k) \\  & =-2i+3j \\  & =⟨-2,3,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}|-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|+(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3(2\cdot 0-(-1)(3))-4(0\cdot 0-(-1)(-2))+(-2)(0\cdot 3-2\cdot (-2)) \\  & =-3(3)-4(-2)-2(4) \\  & =-9-8+8 \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-9|=9.
$$
